newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices quiet as market slips.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices quiet as market slips.

text.p: Major U.S. stock index options trading was relatively quiet Wednesday as the market struggled with early gains only to move lower in afternoon action.
"We've done hardly any index stuff in the last few days," one options trader said. "Our index business has really dried up."
By 1400 CDT/1900 GMT, the S&P 100 index .OEX was down 5.41 at 830.18, just off its session low. The broader S&P 500 index .SPX lost 3.56 to 846.15 and June S&P 500 futures were down 3.35 at 848.
In the OEX, where the majority of index options trade, the busiest issue was the June 820 put, which traded 2,945 contracts. The June 830 put traded about 2,700.
On the call side, the most active OEX options included the June 830, with turnover of 2,330 and the June 840, with volume of about 2,050.
Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said he was expecting the market to head lower because of heavy equity call buying.
"Equity call buying continues to overwhelm the public's interest in equity puts," he said in an afternoon report.
"Eventually--soon--this investor enthusiasm will lead to lower prices," he said.
At the Chicago Board Options exchange, equity call volume outpaced put volume by 300,624 to 87,998 at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT.
But in the OEX, put volume led call volume 23,037 to 19,738.
Traders generally watch equity put/call volumes more closely as a sentiment indicator because index figures can be distorted by heavy arbitrage and big institutional use.
One options trader said further losses in stocks would be linked to action in bonds.

"If the bond market continues to slide, you'll probably see some asset allocation going into bonds," out of stocks, he said. As bond prices fall, yields rise, making them more attractive to some investors.
Stocks powered higher earlier in the week despite weak bonds as strength in technology stocks boosted the broad market.
But that strength was largely absent Wednesday, with the Nasdaq composite index .IXIC losting 3.63 to 1,405.58 after closing at a record high on Tuesday.
The action in technology stocks appeared to boost interest in options on the Morgan Stanley high tech index .MSH, which trade on the American Stock Exchange.
The MSH June 425 call traded 1,900 contracts and the July 445 call traded 3,650.
"It looked like some kind of spread," one trader said. "I would assume they were done as a package."

Another trader said some of his customers had been inquiring about options on the Morgan Stanley multinational index .NFT as a substitute for the OEX because premium levels are lower on an absolute price basis.
